response.sql:
WITH matched AS (
  SELECT f.feesnode, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate, NULLIF(o.mktnote, '') AS pair
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
),
pair_avg AS (
  SELECT pair, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net
  FROM matched
  GROUP BY pair
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(net_rate) AS bench FROM matched
),
kept AS (
  SELECT p.pair, p.avg_net, p.avg_net - b.bench AS excess
  FROM pair_avg p
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE p.avg_net > b.bench
)
SELECT AVG(avg_net) AS avg_of_pair_avg_net,
       AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark
FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique, so the join does not duplicate fee rows. The schema only makes orderspivot the primary key, though the documentation calls recordvault a unique reference.
A missing trading pair means mktnote is NULL or an empty string; NULLIF maps both to one NULL group.
A fee record's net rate is feerate - rebrate. If either value is NULL, the net rate is NULL and is skipped in every average, so it does not count as zero.
Order matching uses plain text equality with no trimming or case folding, as the request asks for exact comparison.

The benchmark is the plain average of net rates over all matched fee records, and each pair's average uses the same net-rate definition. If no matched record has a non-NULL net rate, the benchmark is NULL and the query returns NULL for both results.
